correctness.rationale: Matching closure is idempotent and union-preserving; after compressing identical consecutive matching snapshots, each initially occupied first-matching edge infects exactly a cyclic interval of length \(\min(2r,2m)\). These intervals cover a component exactly when cyclic occupied-edge gaps are \(\le r\). A marked occupied edge and bounded compositions give \(C_{m,r}(s)\), and \(2z+z^2\) tracks exact nonempty endpoint choices, proving the full polynomial. Minimum cardinality and multiplicity follow from least \(s\) with \(sr\ge m\). Bernoulli independence yields the exact distribution; standard disjoint-block lower and union-bound upper estimates prove the logarithmic scale. The standalone actual program checked 648 schedule/family cases and 257976 initial subsets; finite experiments are supporting only. Underlying singular-limit assumptions \(p\in(0,1)\) and component independence are explicit.

value.rationale: This natural time-varying matching family is a meaningful tractable benchmark of a recently introduced computationally difficult temporal forcing problem. The complete all-cardinality seed-set polynomial and exact success characterization are stronger than a single minimal size. They remain valid for arbitrary pairs of perfect matchings with overlaps, any number of alternating-cycle components and arbitrary schedule holding durations; the exact final-state invariance sharply separates switches from elapsed time. The probability and logarithmic random-switching scale are direct useful consequences for spread/reliability analysis, not arbitrary parameter substitutions. No paper-sized result is required for a natural exact classification.
